significant methodological pattern.

4. Non-discriminating arithmetic. The eclipse formula ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF (sub-point 1) is not specific to a dome model. The same arithmetic structure — a station-level magnitude scaled linearly with eclipse coverage through a per-station geometric weight — falls out of a coverage-scaled Chapman-Sq-dynamo treatment fit on the same observational corpus of past eclipses, with the dome's W004 baseline (−22.24 nT, fit to a single 2017 event) playing the role of an empirically-fit Sq amplitude and FSF playing the role of a station-geometry weight. Because the arithmetic is shared, a "Pass" of the dome's codified magnitude pass-band cannot arbitrate between the two interpretations — an August 2026 measurement landing inside the band is equally consistent with coverage-scaled Chapman-Sq as with the dome's W004 recalibration. The structural form of this argument lives at §8b.3 (d)(ii) in the audit-layers framing; §6.14 assumes it and proceeds. A magnitude-only pass-band is a legitimate auditable falsification pattern — the dome is right to want a mechanical rule — but discrimination requires arithmetic the globe cannot reproduce. The escape — a per-station FSF derived from non-Chapman dome physics that produces different magnitudes than Chapman-Sq at the same coverage — is not published in predictions.html, monitor.py, or scripts/fsf_derivation.py. Until it is, the pass-band tests a magnitude both models compute the same way.

Negative evidence: no per-station FSF derivation distinguishing dome from Chapman-Sq is published in predictions.html, monitor.py, or scripts/fsf_derivation.py. The current §4.2.4 (E-PRED-B / FSF = tan(latitude) derivation) and §4.2.5 sub-point 1 (FSF "not independently verifiable") jointly establish that the FSF computation is either trigonometric (tan(lat)) or κ-bearing (the monitor.py track), neither of which is a non-Chapman dome derivation that produces different magnitudes from Chapman-Sq at the same coverage.

anticipated_objections.objection: A dome defender will say Chapman-Sq is not actually arithmetically equivalent to W004 × coverage × FSF — Chapman-Sq is a physics model with a derivation, while the dome's formula is a multiplicative scaling. The shared-arithmetic claim is therefore strawmanning Chapman by reducing it to a linear scaling.
anticipated_objections.response: The argument is about the magnitude-band fit, not the underlying derivation. The published Chapman-Sq predictions (Meza et al. 2021 arXiv:2107.12327, the Kim & Chang 2018 207-measurement ensemble cited in §4.2.2 and §6.14, and the Strestík/Hvožďara/Curto 1999-eclipse multi-site fits) all produce station-level magnitudes that are well-approximated by a baseline × coverage × geometry-weight functional form when one fits the per-station amplitudes to past observations. The point is not that Chapman-Sq IS "baseline × coverage × FSF" in derivation — it is that the per-station magnitudes Chapman-Sq predicts, fit on the same observational corpus the dome fits its W004 baseline against, sit in the same numerical band the dome's W004 × coverage × FSF formula produces. A magnitude-only pass-band cannot tell the two apart by construction. The dome's discriminator would require a published per-station residual structure (phase, time-evolution, coupling to other ionospheric proxies) where Chapman-Sq predicts something the dome predicts differently. No such residual structure is published.

anticipated_objections.objection: The 80-word draft the curmudgeon recommended ("4. Non-discriminating arithmetic. The eclipse formula ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF applied to the W004 recalibration is arithmetically equivalent to a coverage-scaled Chapman-Sq-dynamo treatment of the same observational corpus...") is shorter and crisper. Why land a 230-word version?
anticipated_objections.response: The 80-word version states the conclusion but does not (i) name the W004 baseline value (−22.24 nT) that grounds the argument in the dome's own published parameter, (ii) cross-reference §8b.3 (d)(ii) where the structural form of the argument lives, (iii) acknowledge the kernel of truth (a magnitude-only pass-band IS a legitimate auditable falsification pattern), or (iv) close the escape hatch (a non-Chapman dome FSF derivation). All four elements raise the argument from "assertion" to "audit-quality argument", matching the depth of sub-points 1, 2, and 3 in §4.2.5 (each ~75–100 words, all citing specific dome parameters or paths). 230 words is at the upper edge but consistent with §4.2.5's depth budget for an argument that anchors three other sections (§6.14, §8b.3, §9.2 per part2b cross-reference).

anticipated_objections.objection: The cross-ref to §8b.3 (d)(ii) creates a soft cycle — §8b.3 also references §4.2.5 (and §4.2.4, §4.2.3, §6.14). Won't a reader bounce between the two without finding the canonical statement?
anticipated_objections.response: The cycle is intentional and load-bearing: §4.2.5 is the input-chain home (this is where the baseline × coverage × FSF arithmetic was first analytically dissected in sub-point 1), and §8b.3 (d)(ii) is the audit-layers home (where the same argument is framed as a Pass-band conclusion in a 4-layer eclipse-audit format). Each section needs the other for completeness. The new sub-point 4 explicitly names the relationship: "The structural form of this argument lives at §8b.3 (d)(ii) in the audit-layers framing" — a reader following that link from §4.2.5 arrives at §8b.3 (d)(ii) and finds an audit-form restatement, not a pointer further away. The §6.14 pointer ("this section assumes that argument and proceeds") consumes the argument as a premise; it does not need to be cross-referenced from §4.2.5 because §6.14 is the downstream consumer, not the canonical home. Curmudgeon SEC-8b.3.c10 hole #3 (carry-over from c9 hole #2) is the parallel "§8b.3 cross-references §6.14 for internal formula heterogeneity, but §6.14 doesn't carry that audit" finding and is tracked separately; that hole does not interact with this one.

anticipated_objections.objection: Sub-point 4 says the FSF discrimination escape "is not published in predictions.html, monitor.py, or scripts/fsf_derivation.py." But §4.2.4 already discussed the fsf_derivation.py contents (FSF = tan(latitude) / tan(ref_lat)). Doesn't that contradict the "not published" claim?
anticipated_objections.response: No — the §4.2.4 analysis shows what scripts/fsf_derivation.py DOES publish (FSF = tan(latitude) / tan(ref_lat)), which is a pure trigonometric station-weight that has no Chapman-distinguishing content. The sub-point 4 "not published" claim is narrower: no FSF derivation that produces different MAGNITUDES from Chapman-Sq at the same coverage is published. tan(latitude)/tan(ref_lat) is a station-geometry weight that Chapman-Sq treatments also apply (latitude-dependent ionospheric current geometry); it does not differentiate dome physics from Chapman physics. The monitor.py KAPPA-squared track (analyzed in §6.14) substitutes κ = 1.672 for the tan-derived FSF, producing a different magnitude — but the dome's own defender-pivot in §8b.3 narrows the audit to predictions.html (not monitor.py), and predictions.html publishes the W004 path with tan-FSF. The sub-point 4 wording is precise on this distinction: the escape would be a NON-Chapman derivation, which the published FSF is not.

anticipated_objections.objection: Why doesn't the new sub-point cite the §4.2.2 5–25 nT Chapman magnitude band directly? That would give a reader the numerical evidence that the dome's W004 −22.24 nT lands inside the Chapman band.
anticipated_objections.response: Considered and dropped to keep the sub-point focused on the ARITHMETIC-STRUCTURE argument, not the magnitude-overlap argument. The magnitude-overlap point (W004 at −22.24 nT sits inside the Chapman 5–25 nT band) is already made in §4.2.2 ("globe predicts 5–25 nT, dome predicts ~22 nT, the dome's rule treats 0 nT as globe baseline so the overlap goes unstated") and §6.14 ("W004's −22.24 nT is ~1.5× the upper edge of the Kim & Chang 2018 typical totality ensemble (5–15 nT)"). Sub-point 4 is the structural argument that even if magnitudes match exactly, the test still cannot discriminate because the arithmetic generating them is the same. Adding the magnitude-overlap data would dilute the structural point and duplicate content readers can find one click away.

kernel_of_truth: A magnitude-only pass-band is a legitimate auditable falsification pattern. The dome is right to want a mechanical rule rather than a free-form interpretation — explicit numerical thresholds are the gold standard for falsifiability, and the dome's codification of a magnitude band (±3 nT of 0 nT in the original pre-W004 form; the W004 −22.24 nT central value in the current form) is methodologically sound on its own terms. What the dome did NOT do is choose arithmetic that the globe cannot also reproduce. The pass-band test is a real falsification rule; it just happens to test a number both models compute the same way. The kernel survives: codifying magnitude bands is good methodology. The audit lands: the chosen magnitude does not discriminate.
